dedupe_keys.name: dynamo dynamic climate impact adaptation model agent based model of household flood adaptation insurance and risk under climate change v33

description: DYNAMO is an agent-based model developed at the Institute for Environmental Studies of VU University Amsterdam by Lars de Ruig and Toon Haer to study how households adapt to flood risk as climate and policy change. The Zenodo record read on 2026-09-28 publishes version V33 of the model code, released in August 2022 as a small archive, and lists the studies that used it, whose titles were checked through Crossref: an evaluation of reforms to the US National Flood Insurance Program benchmarked for Jamaica Bay in New York City (Risk Analysis, 2022), a European Union study of the "safe development paradox" in flood risk under climate change (Global Environmental Change, 2020), and a 2019 paper on integrating dynamic adaptive behaviour into risk assessments (Environmental Research Letters), plus a 2022 Nature Climate Change article. Coverage depends on the application, from a New York bay to the European Union. The code is free under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence stated on the record. Caveats: the archive was not opened, so the programming language, required hazard data and documentation are unknown, and an attribution licence is unusual for code. It supports flood adaptation and insurance studies, such as testing how premium reforms change household floodproofing and long-run damage to buildings. No related flood adaptation agent-based model record is catalogued.
